quote: I'm not gonna put it on my roof.
schema_reference: protocols (non-standard scenario handling — not explicitly documented)
stewart_read: This is a genuinely non-standard scenario: ground-mount on an unfinished agricultural structure. The rep improvises alone rather than pausing to consult a supervisor or escalation path, which the schema's non_standard_scenario_hold category exists to catch even though this call shows the omission of a hold rather than an observed hold itself.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: the rep is simply following his own judgment reasonably well given no ground-mount script exists. Strategic read: the rep should have flagged this as outside the standard flow and either escalated or set a firm structured follow-up rather than free-improvising for six minutes.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep on when to pause and check with a manager/supervisor when a lead's install scenario falls outside roof-mount qualification — this call needed that escalation and didn't get it.

quote: I need to know how much it's gonna cost, then I'll know what direction to go.
stewart_read: The customer is essentially asking for a price-before-design, the schema's classic rebuttals.price_estimate_before_design trigger. The rep never uses the canonical redirect-to-design strategy or ties it back to bill/usage data — he instead treats the ask as blocked by construction timing.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be trying to avoid overpromising on an unbuildable ground-mount scenario. But this doesn't require skipping the redirect-to-design script entirely — the redirect could still apply.
coaching_implication: Rep should have used the price_estimate_before_design rebuttal strategy: acknowledge the ask, explain design depends on usage data, and use that as the reason to collect the bill now rather than waiting.

quote: I just need some prices so I know which way to go.
stewart_read: This is the second time the customer states the identical blocking need for pricing information, and the rep again fails to use it as leverage to collect the bill or usage data — he instead reiterates the structural limitation ('the other one's not finished yet').
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep just didn't recognize the repetition as a pattern worth addressing differently the second time. No strong strategic counter-read exists — repeating the same non-answer twice is a miss both times.
coaching_implication: When a customer repeats the same ask, that's the signal to change tactics, not repeat the same deflection — replay both instances with the rep.

quote: I even thought about, digging down in the ground and, putting down, pipe in the ground and and, and do my act condition like that.
stewart_read: The customer drifts into an extended, unmanaged tangent (geothermal HVAC, chicken heaters, greenhouse wiring) spanning nearly a full minute with no redirection from the rep. This isn't a cross-sell signal so much as unmanaged scope-drift — the rep lets the call wander rather than steering back to qualification or a bill/usage anchor.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be letting the customer talk to build rapport before redirecting. But no redirect ever comes — the call ends shortly after without returning to qualification, so the rapport-building read isn't supported by what follows.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep on redirecting long tangents back to the qualification path within a set time window, rather than passively riding along until the call fizzles.

quote: I need more energy up and this ice and snow melts off.
stewart_read: The customer casually reveals he's already running 220V service to a greenhouse and heating chicken coops electrically — both signs of unusually high or growing electric load, which is a strong qualification signal for solar sizing. The rep never picks up on this as bill/usage-anchor material.
coaching_implication: This kind of detail (multiple electric-heavy structures on the property) should have been flagged as evidence of high usage and tied into a bill-collection ask — instead it passed by as background chatter.

quote: Well, maybe I can try calling back some other time then.
stewart_read: The rep ends the substantive part of the call with a vague callback promise and no date, time, or commitment mechanism — no 'is that fair' handshake, no specific day. This is a procedural exit failure distinct from the underlying non-standard scenario.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: connection quality genuinely degraded (customer's phone breaking up), which limits how much the rep could lock down. Strategic read doesn't hold here — even amid bad connection, no attempt at a specific date was made earlier in the call when the connection was still clear (e.g., at 03:11 or 04:10).
coaching_implication: Even in scenarios blocked on customer-side construction timing, the rep should propose a specific week/date for the follow-up rather than an open-ended 'some other time.'

quote: I'm not I'm not gonna have anybody to install it. I'm only install it myself.
stewart_read: Self-installation is very likely a hard disqualifier for Ion (a licensed-installer company), but the rep responds with uncertainty ('I don't know if you'd be able to help out really') instead of clearly stating Ion's install model or escalating to confirm. This is a genuine knowledge gap, not a scope-creep or scam issue.
coaching_implication: Rep needs a clear, confident answer for self-install requests — either a firm 'we handle installation ourselves' disqualifier or a defined escalation path — rather than an ambiguous non-answer.
